text: That sounds like classic angina. Have you noticed any changes in your risk factors, such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or a family history of heart disease? Also, do you smoke or consume alcohol regularly?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been managing high blood pressure for ten years and have high cholesterol, and I do smoke about a pack a day. I don't have diabetes, but my father did have heart disease. I only drink socially, so I don't consume alcohol regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: That combination of risk factors significantly increases your likelihood of coronary artery disease. Have you experienced any chest pain while at rest, or has the frequency of these episodes increased recently? REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG) REQUEST TEST: Lipid_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram: ST segment depression in leads I, AVL, V4-V6 suggestive of ischemia. Lipid Panel: Total Cholesterol 250 mg/dL (elevated), LDL 160 mg/dL (elevated), HDL 40 mg/dL, Triglycerides 180 mg/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ECG confirms ischemia, and your lipid panel shows significant dyslipidemia. Have you ever experienced a sudden, severe tearing pain in your chest or back, or any fainting spells during these episodes? REQUEST TEST: Troponin_Level REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: The troponin and echocardiogram results are reassuring, which helps rule out an acute heart attack or structural heart failure. Given your history of exertional pain radiating to the jaw and arm, along with confirmed ischemia on the ECG, do you have any history of heartburn, acid reflux, or pain that improves with antacids?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't have any history of heartburn or acid reflux, and the pain I feel does not improve with antacids. It is strictly related to my physical exertion and goes away when I rest.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stable Angina Pectoris secondary to Coronary Artery Disease.
